rubrics.justification: The response conflicts with the provided lab grade of 3AB by reclassifying the embryo as 4BB, downgrading the ICM and upgrading the TE. It includes detailed morphology, but key grading elements appear inaccurate relative to the case data.
It thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, endometriosis, semen quality, endometrial thickness, cycle history, and transfer timing with embryo quality and prognosis.

The reasoning is generally logical and structured, with a clear link from embryo quality and patient factors to prognosis. Minor issues include somewhat speculative quantitative adjustments for stress and endometriosis.

Many recommendations are standard and evidence-based, including SET and routine luteal support, but some suggestions are weakly supported or overstated for routine use (extended progesterone for endometriosis, ERA, acupuncture, broad adjunct supplements, surgery/PGT-A without stronger indication).

Provides practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including SET, luteal support, monitoring, and future options. Some recommendations are useful but not all are equally evidence-based or necessary in this first-cycle setting.
